eras.eraTitle: Dynastic Dawn in the Malnad Hills
eras.description: Originating in the hill tracts of Angadi (Sasakapura) in the Western Ghats, early Hoysala chieftains served as Western Chalukyan feudatories. The foundational lore recounts young prince Sala striking down a leaping tiger on the command of his Jain ascetic guru ('Poy Sala!' — 'Strike, Sala!'), establishing the royal dynasty and emblem.

milestones.title: Early Hill Stronghold Established
milestones.summary: Nripa Kama II establishes territorial influence in Chikkamagaluru hills as a Western Chalukya tributary.

milestones.title: Capital Shifted to Dwarasamudra (Halebidu)
milestones.summary: Vinayaditya strengthens administration and establishes Dwarasamudra amid deep irrigation tanks.

eras.description: Vishnuvardhana's military conquest of Talakadu from the Chola viceroys in 1116 triggered an architectural revolution. The king, guided by Sri Ramanujacharya, embraced Srivaishnavism while maintaining eclectic patronage of Shaivism and Jainism, commissioning monumental temples in soft chloritic schist.

milestones.title: Consecration of Lakshmi Devi Temple
milestones.summary: Doddagaddavalli's rare quadruple (chatuskuta) sanctuary founded by merchant-patron Kulla and his wife Sahaja Devi.

milestones.title: Royal Dedication of Belur Chennakeshava
milestones.summary: Consecration of the ekakuta Vijayanarayana (Chennakeshava) temple at Belur to commemorate triumph at Talakadu.

milestones.title: Foundation of Halebidu Hoysaleswara
milestones.summary: Construction begins on the colossal dvikuta double Shiva sanctuary under high officer Ketamalla.

eras.eraTitle: Imperial Sovereign Expansion under Ballala II
eras.description: Veera Ballala II declared total independence from the weakening Western Chalukyas, defeating the Kalachuris and Sevunas. Royal officers, generals (dandanayakas), and queens sponsored jewel-like temples featuring hyper-refined lathe-turned pillars and multi-banded narrative friezes across Karnataka.

milestones.title: Brahmeshvara Temple at Kikkeri
milestones.summary: Commissioned by royal patroness Bammaladevi, exhibiting curved vimana contours.

milestones.title: Buchesvara Temple at Koravangala
milestones.summary: Dedicated by royal officer Buchiraja on the exact coronation day of King Veera Ballala II.

milestones.title: Amrutesvara Temple at Amruthapura
milestones.summary: Amrutheshwara Dandanayaka commissions a sprawling temple featuring 140 ceiling panels depicting the epics.

milestones.title: Veera Narayana Temple at Belavadi
milestones.summary: A grand trikuta sanctuary dedicated to Vishnu forms, built on an expansive stone platform.

milestones.title: Ishvara Temple at Arasikere
milestones.summary: Celebrated for its complex 16-point star open natyamandapa hall capped with a domical ceiling.

eras.description: During the mid-to-late thirteenth century, the Hoysala court achieved mathematical perfection in trikuta stellate sanctuaries. Signed master sculptors, most notably Ruvari Mallitamma, covered entire temple enclosures with lace-like narrative reliefs and miniature vimana spires.

milestones.title: Mallikarjuna Temple at Basaralu
milestones.summary: Harihara Dandanayaka dedicates a rich trikuta temple carrying exquisite Mahabharata friezes.

milestones.title: Lakshminarasimha Temple at Javagal
milestones.summary: Trikuta temple with extensive wall carvings attributed to the workshop of Mallitamma.

milestones.title: Lakshminarayana Temple at Hosaholalu
milestones.summary: Fine trikuta plan with deeply undercut friezes and ornate ceiling coffers.

milestones.title: Chennakesava Temple at Aralaguppe
milestones.summary: Compact stellate shrine featuring one of Karnataka's finest Ugra Narasimha wall relief sculptures.

milestones.title: Consecration of Somanathapura Chennakesava
milestones.summary: High commander Somanatha Dandanayaka consecrates a textbook trikuta masterpiece enclosed in a cloistered courtyard.

eras.eraTitle: The Crucible Era & Transition to Vijayanagara
eras.description: In 1311 and 1327, armies of the Delhi Sultanate under Malik Kafur and Muhammad bin Tughlaq raided and devastated the Hoysala capital of Dwarasamudra. King Veera Ballala III relocated his defensive court, organizing fierce resistance across southern India until falling at the Battle of Madurai in 1343. His commanders and artisans provided the direct administrative and architectural foundation for the emerging Vijayanagara Empire.

milestones.title: First Sacking of Dwarasamudra
milestones.summary: Malik Kafur's expedition forces concessions from King Ballala III, damaging outer city walls.

milestones.title: Fall of Ballala III & Rise of Vijayanagara
milestones.summary: Following Ballala III's demise, Hoysala territory, master stone guilds, and defenses merge into the Sangama brothers' fledgling Vijayanagara state.
